subject: Mathematical Physics
learning_objectives: Represent vectors in Cartesian components and unit-vector bases.
Use dot and cross products for projections, angles, areas and torque.
Use scalar and vector triple products and interpret their geometry.
Recognize vector-product identities and common CSIR-NET traps.

theory.heading: Vectors and components
theory.content: A = A_x i + A_y j + A_z k. Its magnitude is |A| = sqrt(A_x^2 + A_y^2 + A_z^2). A unit vector is A_hat = A/|A| for A != 0.

theory.heading: Dot product
theory.content: A·B = |A||B|cos(theta) = A_xB_x + A_yB_y + A_zB_z. It is a scalar. The scalar projection of A on B is A·B_hat.

theory.heading: Cross product
theory.content: A×B is normal to the plane of A and B, with magnitude |A×B| = |A||B|sin(theta). It is anti-commutative: A×B = -B×A.

theory.heading: Scalar triple product
theory.content: A·(B×C) is the signed volume of the parallelepiped formed by A, B and C. It is zero when the vectors are coplanar.

theory.heading: Vector triple product
theory.content: A×(B×C) = B(A·C) - C(A·B). Cross multiplication is not associative.

theory.heading: Physical applications
theory.content: Work by a constant force is W = F·Delta r; torque is tau = r×F; angular momentum is L = r×p.

formula_sheet: Vector projection of A on B = [(A·B)/|B|^2]B

worked_examples.title: Projection
worked_examples.problem: Find the scalar projection of A=(2,-1,2) on B=(1,2,2).
worked_examples.solution: A·B=4 and |B|=3, so the scalar projection is 4/3.

worked_examples.title: Triangle area
worked_examples.problem: Find the area of the triangle formed by A=(1,0,0) and B=(0,2,0).
worked_examples.solution: A×B=(0,0,2), so the triangle area is |A×B|/2 = 1.

worked_examples.title: Coplanarity
worked_examples.solution: C=A+B, so the three vectors are linearly dependent and A·(B×C)=0.

derivations.title: Dot product from components
steps: Write A=A_x i+A_y j+A_z k and B=B_x i+B_y j+B_z k.
Use i·i=j·j=k·k=1 and cross terms zero.

derivations.title: Cross-product magnitude
steps: Therefore area is |A||B|sin(theta), the magnitude of A×B.

part_b_practice.question: If A·B=0 for two nonzero vectors, the angle is:
The magnitude of (i+j)×(i-j) is:
part_b_practice.explanation: The cross product is -2k, whose magnitude is 2.

part_b_practice.question: If A×B=0 for nonzero vectors, they are:
part_b_practice.explanation: sin(theta)=0, so theta is 0 or 180 degrees.

part_b_practice.question: The scalar triple product of three coplanar vectors is:
part_b_practice.explanation: It represents signed volume, which vanishes for coplanar vectors.

part_b_practice.question: Which identity is correct?
part_b_practice.explanation: This is the vector triple-product identity.

part_c_practice.question: A force F=3i+4j acts at r=2i-j. Find torque about the origin.
For A=(1,1,0), B=(1,0,1), find a unit vector perpendicular to both.

common_mistakes: Confusing scalar projection with vector projection.
Using sin(theta) for the dot product.
Dropping absolute values for geometric area/volume.

When the vectors are parallel/anti-parallel or one is zero.

The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by A, B and C.

revision.one_minute: Dot -> angle/projection/work. Cross -> normal/area/torque. Triple product -> volume/coplanarity.
